Expense: research, brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists, training (human capital). Asset: development costs meeting IAS 38 criteria, software, patents.

Research: new knowledge → expense. Development: apply knowledge to new/improved products before production → capitalise when criteria met (feasibility, intention, ability, probable benefits, resources, reliable cost); amortise from launch.
Purchase price + directly attributable costs (transport, installation, testing). Not: training, celebrations, general overhead.

Cost model: cost − accumulated depreciation − impairment (standard in Europe). Revaluation model: fair value (intangibles only with an active market, e.g. taxi licences). Component approach for significant parts.
Finite life (licence, patent): amortise. Indefinite life (goodwill, brands): no amortisation, impairment test at least annually.

PPE/finite-life intangibles: only if indications (market value decline, adverse changes, interest rates, obsolescence, damage, worse performance). Goodwill/indefinite-life intangibles: at least annually.
Higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use. Impairment loss = carrying amount − recoverable amount (expense). New depreciation on the reduced amount.
PV of future pre-tax cash flows from use and disposal (max. ~5 years of forecasts), excluding financing and tax; pre-tax discount rate (or WACC).
Smallest group of assets generating cash inflows largely independent of others (store, magazine title, plant). Used when an asset's cash flows cannot be determined individually.
1 goodwill · 2 other assets pro rata to carrying amounts. No asset below max(FV less costs to sell, value in use, 0).
Required when indications disappear; capped at the carrying amount without impairment (depreciated cost). Gain in P/L. Goodwill: never reversed.

Right to control the use of an identified asset for a period in exchange for consideration: identified asset + substantially all economic benefits + right to direct the use. Otherwise: service contract (expense).

Liability = PV of future lease payments (implicit rate or incremental borrowing rate). ROU = liability + payments at/before commencement − incentives + initial direct costs + dismantling costs. Then: depreciation of ROU (shorter of term and useful life) + interest; payments reduce the liability.
Lessee only: short-term (≤ 12 months) and low-value (≈ USD 5,000) leases → straight-line expense + disclosure. Lessor: still finance vs operating lease (no big change).
Under IFRS 16 both create an asset (PPE/ROU) and financial debt, both generate depreciation + interest. Leasing is no longer off-balance-sheet financing → gearing increases too.
